title: Divide and Conquer Check
description: Identify divide, conquer, combine and cost patterns.

questions.prompt: The three classic divide-and-conquer steps are:
questions.explanation: Split the input (divide), solve pieces recursively (conquer), then merge partial answers (combine).

questions.prompt: If each recursion level does `O(n)` work and there are `O(log n)` levels from halving, total time is often:
questions.explanation: That pattern (Merge Sort story) is often `O(n log n)`: `O(n)` work per level × `O(log n)` levels.

questions.prompt: Why can teaching code that `slice`s halves each call be costly?

options.text: It allocates new arrays each call — extra copying cost
It prevents the base case from running

questions.explanation: `arr.slice` allocates new arrays each call. Production divide-and-conquer usually passes index ranges to avoid extra copying.

options.text: A heavy merge of two sorted halves each step
A cheap / no heavy combine — discard one half

questions.explanation: Binary search is divide-and-conquer without a heavy combine: you keep one half. Combine cost matters — cheap vs merge of sorted halves.
